absent: Permission bitmask table layout and fault-error-code encoding values.
PKRU enforcement interaction with EPT versus shadow paging beyond mask construction.
TDP MMU root reference counting and put-root teardown effects.
MMIO SPTE detection rule and non-present replacement value layout.
Child-parent link structures and parent detach TLB interaction.
Unsync page synchronization trigger and content.
Handling of broadcast TLB flush and obsolete-root free requests on the vCPU exit path.
Lifetime of current versus previous roots, full root bitmask values, and dummy root creation.
Numeric ABI values for page-fault masks, page levels, huge-page shifts, and EPT control bits.

findings.text: Unload operation releases all roots for both the active root MMU and the guest MMU of a vCPU and clears any cached MMIO address information, warning if root state remains valid afterwards.

Root release selects current and previous roots by bitmask, skips locking when no selected root is valid, otherwise frees previous roots and the active root including dummy, shadow and four-entry PAE cases, then resets root identifiers.
Page-walk permission data is refreshed from translation mode selectors for two-dimensional paging and extended page tables together with current SMEP, SMAP, write-protect and no-execute controls.

Protection-key mask is cleared and left zero when protection keys are disabled; when enabled it encodes per fault-code combinations so that only non-fetch accesses to user pages check keys, write checks additionally require user fault or write-protect, access-disable blocks read and write while write-disable blocks write.

Root freeing holds the VM MMU lock in read mode for direct TDP roots and in write mode otherwise; TDP path requires no deferred zap list on unlock while the shadow path commits the collected zap list before releasing the write lock.

Individual root teardown expects read protection for TDP pages and write protection for shadow pages, decrements shadow root references and queues the page for zapping only when the last reference disappears and the page is already marked invalid.

Zap preparation increments accounting, zaps unsynchronized children, unlinks children and parents, releases shadow and NX huge-page accounting, detaches unsync state, moves zero-reference pages to the invalid list and marks them invalid, otherwise detaches active roots and requests obsolete-root reclamation.

Guest frame lookup for a shadow page returns the page base for passthrough pages, a shifted cached translation when a shadowed translation array exists, otherwise the base plus entry index scaled by page level.
Shadow presence is determined by testing the entry against the MMU present mask rather than architectural present bits.

Remote TLB flush accounts a request, publishes page-table changes before observing vCPU modes, attempts an architecture-specific flush and falls back to a broadcast flush request, accounting a completed flush when either path acted.

Broadcast request walks online vCPUs through the vCPU array bounded by the online count, records the request on each vCPU, attempts wakeup, accumulates CPUs needing an interrupt, issues them together, and reports whether any kick was sent.

Need for an interrupt is derived from an atomic transition of vCPU mode from in-guest to exiting-guest: waiting requests need it unless outside guest mode, non-waiting requests need it only when in guest mode.
Recording a request orders prior stores before setting the request bit; wakeup uses architecture-selected wait state, marks readiness and accounts halt wakeups when the wait queue was active.

Guest frame to slot translation first retries the cached last-used slot when the frame lies within its range, otherwise walks the guest-frame tree by base and size, updating the cache on hit and returning null on miss unless approximate lookup is allowed.

Large-page permission is tracked per slot and level by adjusting disallow counters from 2M up to the maximum huge level; write tracking adjusts a per-frame counter and, on removal, restores large-page permission, with lookups indexed by frame offset from slot base.

Write-track removal requires MMU write protection plus slot or SRCU protection, validates that tracking is active, decrements the frame counter and re-enables large pages; tracking is active when external tracking is enabled, a shadow root exists, or two-dimensional paging is disabled.
Shadow unaccounting decrements indirect page counts, resolves the owning slot, removes write tracking for pages above 4K and otherwise restores large-page mapping.

Committed zapping must flush remote TLBs before freeing so that lockless walkers and guest entries observe table changes; freeing validates that pages are invalid with no remaining root references and, under verification builds, that no entry remains shadow-present.

Observed shadow-page state includes role flags for direct, passthrough, guest mode, level and invalid, guest frame number, root reference count, unsync flag, MMU generation, TDP marker, NX huge-page marker, table pointer, cached translation pointer, hash and active links, parent tracking, possible NX huge-page link and clear counter.

Entry zapping drops last-level present mappings, detaches parent links for table entries, clears MMIO entries without tracking, and recursively zaps unreferenced nested guest-mode children when two-dimensional paging is active.

Fast entry clearing writes a non-present value with ordering that prevents fetching mixed old and new halves on split-entry builds and counts transitions to non-present; virtualization-exception possibility depends on shadow mask configuration, suppress bit and misconfigured write-execute combination.

Unsync detachment clears the flag and decrements unsync accounting; obsolescence holds for invalid pages and for non-TDP pages whose generation mismatches the VM generation; only non-direct non-passthrough pages own guest entries; page accounting releases shadow counts and secondary pagetable charges while NX huge-page untracking updates split statistics.

Bug helper evaluates a condition once, warns once and marks the VM bugged on first trigger, then reports the condition; MMU warning helper either warns once or enforces compile-time validity depending on build variant.
